asOf: 16 November 2026, one day before the IPL 2027 retention deadline
summary: Two gaps stand out in the data: a middle-order batter proven in the crunch, and a second pressure bowler to partner Jofra Archer. Both openers are elite but barely tested at the death, and every squad slot is full, so the plan starts with releases.
confidence: Retention lists were due on 17 November 2026 and were not public when this was compiled, so availability below is a judgement from media reporting.

squad.status: Retained for 2026 (₹1.1 cr). 776 runs in IPL 2026 [S1]
squad.note: Usual level +18.3, the highest of anyone listed, but 0 High-tier balls: unrated at high pressure

squad.name: Yashasvi Jaiswal
squad.status: Retained for 2026 (₹18 cr) [S1]; trade talk reported, a move now described as unlikely [S6]
squad.note: Usual level +6.7; 3 High-tier balls: unrated at high pressure

squad.name: Shimron Hetmyer
squad.status: Widely tipped for release; 78 runs at SR 113 in 2026 [S4][S5]

squad.name: Ravindra Jadeja
squad.status: Traded in from CSK for 2026 (₹14 cr) [S1]
squad.note: Rated 34th of 35 batters (-2.7); not enough High-tier balls to be rated as a bowler

squad.name: Ravi Bishnoi
squad.status: Bought for 2026 (₹7.2 cr) [S1]; lost his place mid-season [S7]
squad.note: Rated 26th of 64 bowlers (+3.2); largest negative lift among Royals (-3.9)

squad.name: Sandeep Sharma
squad.status: Named as a release candidate; economy 11.38 in six 2026 games [S4]
squad.note: Below the eligibility floor; usual level +1.5, lift -2.1

needs.title: A middle-order batter proven in the crunch
needs.detail: All four of the Royals' rated middle-order batters sit in the bottom half of 35: Parag 22nd, Hetmyer 27th, Jurel 29th, Jadeja 34th. Hetmyer, the designated finisher, is the most likely release.
needs.evidence: Primary: outputs/rankings/batters_all.csv. Corroborated by post-season reviews that call the middle order the biggest issue [S7].

needs.title: A second pressure bowler beside Archer
needs.detail: Archer is the only Royals bowler in the top third. Deshpande is 56th of 64 and Sandeep Sharma falls below the floor. An Indian seamer would also free an overseas slot.
needs.evidence: Primary: outputs/rankings/bowlers_all.csv. Reviews: 'the bowling needs one more Indian death-overs option' [S7].

needs.title: Test the openers before paying for certainty
needs.detail: Sooryavanshi and Jaiswal have the two best usual levels in the squad but almost no High-pressure balls, because openers are out or home before the crunch. The data cannot say how they finish chases; it is not a reason to buy, but it is a reason not to assume.

targets.name: Wanindu Hasaranga
targets.availability: Reported: missed all of IPL 2026 injured after joining LSG for ₹2 cr; CricTracker (16 Nov) calls his release 'a realistic option' after LSG traded for Kuldeep Yadav [S8]
targets.why: 9th of 64 bowlers, the highest-rated bowler with a credible route to the auction. 549 pressure balls, 75 in the High tier.
targets.risk: Hamstring injury; overseas slot needed; his own pressure lift was negative (-1.2), which section 5 shows does not predict the future but a selector will see it.

targets.name: Nathan Ellis
targets.availability: Unknown: retained by CSK for 2026 [S9]; no 2027 reporting found
targets.why: 12th of 64 bowlers; the death specialist the Royals have lacked. 33% chance of a true top-10 place.
targets.risk: Overseas; CSK may keep him; availability for the full season.

targets.name: Cameron Green
targets.fit: Top-four or floating middle order, seam bowling
targets.availability: Reported: several outlets name him a likely KKR release on salary and fitness grounds [S10]
targets.why: 8th of 35 batters (+6.2) with 37 High-tier balls; would replace Hetmyer's slot with a higher-rated batter who also bowls.
targets.risk: Price could be very high; injury history; overseas slot.

targets.name: Mohsin Khan
targets.fit: Indian left-arm pace, the Royals' missing profile
targets.availability: Unlikely: no release reporting; LSG managed his workload through 2026 [S11]
targets.why: 8th of 64 bowlers and Indian, so no overseas slot. 11 wickets at 8.14 in seven 2026 games [S11].
targets.risk: Missed IPL 2025 and parts of 2026 injured; would probably need a trade.

targets.name: Bhuvneshwar Kumar
targets.fit: Indian seam, new ball and death
targets.why: 10th of 64 bowlers; the most-tested Indian seamer in the data (738 pressure balls, 127 High-tier).
targets.risk: Age; RCB expected to keep a title-winning core.

targets.name: Sikandar Raza
targets.fit: Spin-bowling all-rounder for the middle order
targets.availability: Likely in the pool: no IPL appearance since 2024 in the data
targets.why: 25th of 35 batters but tested (55 High-tier balls), and he also bowls off-spin.

notAvailable.reason: 13th of 64 bowlers, but the BCCI directed KKR to release him in January 2026 amid political pressure [S13]. Whether he could be signed for 2027 is unclear.

caveats: Availability is the least certain part of this page. Revisit it once the retention lists are published on or after 17 November 2026.
Ratings measure how players performed in this data, 2022 to 2026. They do not account for price, age, fitness, or how a player fits the Jaipur pitch.

The Royals' squad and overseas slots were full at 25 and 8 [S5]. Every target therefore assumes releases first. Releasing Hetmyer, Milne and Shanaka was reported to free ₹15.40 crore and three overseas slots [S5].
Where sources disagreed (Hasaranga's 2026 team, Muzarabani's status), the conflict is noted rather than resolved. Data Pack facts take precedence over media reports.
